user: And I still have time to file, right?
answer:
Probably yes, but the deadline depends on the reason, and some windows are close. Based on today's date in our system (2026-09-15), and counting from the TX-0401 date (2026-07-20), the windows are:

| Reason code | Window | Days left | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duplicate charge | 60 days | 3 | Open, closing soon |
| Unauthorised debit | 56 days | 0 | Closed (day 57) |
| Goods not received | 90 days | 35 | Open |
| Service not rendered | 90 days | 35 | Open |
| Unauthorised card payment | 120 days | 65 | Open |

If this is a duplicate charge, you need to act within about 3 days. Unauthorised debit is no longer available for this transaction. These windows are only a guide. I still have to run the eligibility check, which also looks at transaction status and any account-level restrictions, before anything can be filed.

fragments.text:
Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Limit operations
## Window definition
Limits are tracked on calendar days, not business days. The daily window runs
from 00:00 to 23:59 CET.

Payment dispute rules
## Eligibility conditions
A dispute is eligible only if all of the following hold: the reason code is
valid; the transaction status is settled; the transaction date is within the
reason code's window relative to the current date; and no customer-level
restriction applies (for example, an account under compliance review cannot
open new disputes until the review concludes).
